we propose a new method for training transition policies for complex tasks that smoothly connect lower level policies by matching their distributions, and that we show that this method achieves higher success rates on complex tasks than previous methods.

1) we introduce transition policies that match the distribution of states and action expected by the next lower-level policy; and 2) we use deep Q-networks with a binary action-space to decide when to switch from the transition policy to the lower-level policy.

matching the distribution of states and transitions can be a useful alternative to reward functions for complex tasks.
by matching distributions of states and actions, transition policies can be learned from sparse rewards, enabling the transfer of skills across different subtasks.
training transition policies to match the expected distribution of states and next actions is a promising direction to enable hierarchical reinforcement learning to solve complex tasks.
